sentences.en: I want you to imagine a world where you can just invent a musical instrument.
sentences.zh: 我想请你想象这样一个世界：你可以随心所欲地发明一种乐器。

sentences.en: I don't mean when you were a kid and you put some rubber bands on a tissue box.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是你小时候把橡皮筋绑在纸巾盒上那种玩意儿。

sentences.en: I mean you come up with a new instrument almost from scratch and then watch
sentences.zh: 我是说，你几乎从零开始构思出一种新乐器，然后看着它

sentences.en: as that instrument gets taken up and played in nearly every marching band,
sentences.zh: 被全国几乎所有的行进乐队、

sentences.en: jazz band, and high school music classroom across the country.
sentences.zh: 爵士乐队和高中音乐课堂所采用。

sentences.en: There actually was a time where this kind of thing happened.
sentences.zh: 历史上确实有过一段时期，这种事情真的发生了。

sentences.en: In the 19th century, Western Europe saw an explosion of instrument innovation
sentences.zh: 19世纪的西欧见证了乐器创新的大爆发，

sentences.en: where the entire landscape of instrumentation was shifting
sentences.zh: 整个乐器格局都在发生转变，

sentences.en: and where there was money to be made if your improvements caught on with the public.
sentences.zh: 只要你的改进能被大众接受，就能赚到钱。

sentences.en: This is when many of the instruments we know today reached their modern forMs.
sentences.zh: 许多我们今天熟知的乐器都是在这一时期定型的。

sentences.en: Trumpets had been around since Roman times,
sentences.zh: 小号从罗马时代就存在了，

sentences.en: but in the 19th century they took on the valved form we know today
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪，它们演变成了我们今天所知的活塞式结构，

sentences.en: and flutes went from being conical wooden instruments to metal cylinders.
sentences.zh: 长笛也从圆锥形的木制乐器变成了金属圆柱体。

sentences.en: But one of the greatest innovations to come out of this time was the saxophone.
sentences.zh: 但那个时代最伟大的创新之一就是萨克斯风。

sentences.en: The saxophone wasn't an improvement on a previous instrument.
sentences.zh: 萨克斯风并不是对原有乐器的改良。

sentences.en: It was a brand new invention.
A hybrid of brass and woodwind that not only managed to secure a spot in the musical canon,
sentences.zh: 这是一种铜管与木管的混合体，它不仅在音乐经典中占有一席之地，

sentences.en: but also went on to change American music forever.
sentences.zh: 还永远地改变了美国音乐。

sentences.en: It's design came from the mind of a brash young entrepreneur.
sentences.zh: 它的设计出自一位年轻气盛的企业家之手。

sentences.en: His name, perhaps unsurprisingly, was Saxe.
sentences.zh: 他的名字，或许并不令人惊讶，叫萨克斯。

sentences.en: Adolphe Saxe was born in Dinant, Belgium, in 1814.
sentences.zh: 阿道夫·萨克斯于1814年出生在比利时的迪南。

sentences.en: His full name was actually Antoine-Joseph Saxe,
sentences.zh: 他的全名其实是安托万-约瑟夫·萨克斯，

sentences.en: but at the time Adolphe wasn't, you know, taken.
sentences.zh: 但当时“阿道夫”这个名字还没被占用，你知道的。

sentences.en: So he went by that instead.
sentences.zh: 所以他就用了这个名字。

sentences.en: It's difficult not to remember him as this romanticised figure.
sentences.zh: 很难不把他看作一个充满浪漫色彩的人物。

sentences.en: The rags to riches to rags, the fiery temper.
sentences.zh: 从贫穷到富有再到贫穷的经历，还有那火爆的脾气。
这位是斯蒂芬·科特雷尔博士，

sentences.en: because Saxe nearly died before he invented anything.
sentences.zh: 因为萨克斯在发明任何东西之前差点就死了。

sentences.en: Adolphe Saxe was the eldest of 11 children,
sentences.zh: 阿道夫·萨克斯是11个孩子中的长子，

sentences.en: only four of whom made it to age 30,

sentences.en: so the odds were stacked against young Adolphe from the start.

he apparently nearly died as a kid.
sentences.zh: 那些差点让他丧命的经历之前，我得先深吸一口气。

sentences.en: He fell three flights of stairs and cracked his head on a stone floor.
sentences.zh: 他从三层楼高的楼梯上摔下来，头撞在石地板上裂开了。

probably what we would call sulfuric acid today,

sentences.en: He was burned in a gunpowder explosion,

sentences.en: and then again when a frying pan was knocked over.
sentences.zh: 后来又因为平底锅被打翻再次被烧伤。

sentences.en: A stone fell off a roof and left a lifelong scar on his head.
